title: Integral schemes: sections and stalks inject into the function field
statement:
Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point] (so $\overline{\{\eta\}}=X$, and $\eta$ lies in every nonempty open subset of $X$) and function field $k(X)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ [def-sc-function-field], a field. For $x\in X$ let $\rho_x:\mathcal O_{X,x}\to k(X)$ be the ring map of stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] sending the germ $s_x$ of a section $s\in\mathcal O_X(W)$, $W$ an open neighbourhood of $x$, to its germ $s_\eta$ (well defined since $\eta\in W$). Then:

1. for every open $V\subseteq X$ and every $x\in V$ the germ map $\mathcal O_X(V)\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $s\mapsto s_x$, is injective;
2. for every $x\in X$ the ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is an integral domain, $\rho_x$ is injective, and $\rho_x$ makes $k(X)$ a field of fractions of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$: every element of $k(X)$ is $\rho_x(a)\rho_x(b)^{-1}$ with $a,b\in\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $b\neq0$.

In particular for a nonempty open $V$ and $x\in V$ the composite $\mathcal O_X(V)\to\mathcal O_{X,x}\to k(X)$, which is $s\mapsto s_\eta$, is injective.
